## Summary

The 2026-05-03 [[stripe]] guide describes [[stripe-p24|Przelewy24 (P24)]] as a single-use payment method that redirects customers to authenticate. It covers Checkout, iOS, Android, React Native, and legacy Elements. At the same guide URL, the 2026-11-07 capture lists links to those five variants. The implementation details below come from the May capture.

## Key Details

### Checkout

- The May compatibility table lists EUR and PLN. Checkout Sessions use payment mode and accept only one-time line items. All line items in a Session must have the same currency. Create separate Sessions for different currencies.
- Stripe can select eligible methods dynamically. The separate manual instructions say to include `p24` in `payment_method_types` and use EUR for all line items. The May examples use `success_url` for Stripe-hosted Checkout and `return_url` for embedded Checkout.
- To test Checkout, select P24 and click Pay. The May guide documents refunds up to 180 days after the original payment and says there is no dispute process.
- May raw lines 12–50 cover eligibility and method selection, 52–103 cover hosted and embedded examples, and 105–117 cover fulfillment, testing, refunds, and disputes.

### Mobile PaymentIntents

In the May mobile examples, the server creates a PaymentIntent with the amount, EUR or PLN, and `p24`, then passes the client secret to the app. All three examples instruct the app to collect the customer's email and show it in billing details.

- **iOS** uses `STPPaymentMethodPrzelewy24Params()` and `STPPaymentHandler.confirmPayment()` (May raw lines 221–305).
- **Android** uses `PaymentMethodCreateParams.createP24(billingDetails)` and `PaymentLauncher.confirm()` (May raw lines 406–512).
- **React Native** uses `confirmPayment(clientSecret, { paymentMethodType: 'P24' })`. The guide labels its deep-link section optional and requires a return URL for methods that need one. It shows a custom URL scheme for bank redirects and forwarding the return to the SDK (May raw lines 586–609, 618–729, 757–767).

### Elements (legacy)

- The May guide labels this integration legacy and warns that support could end on deprecation. It specifically says the legacy `p24Bank` element was unavailable in the latest Stripe.js version at the time and recommends the Payment Element (May raw lines 819–825, 892–894).
- In the historical client path, the server creates the PaymentIntent with the amount, EUR or PLN, and `p24`. The client calls `stripe.confirmP24Payment()` with the client secret and a `return_url`. The HTML example supplies customer email in billing details. The two React examples omit it, so the examples leave API requiredness unresolved (May raw lines 840–862, 1055–1095, 1139–1158, 1221–1230).
- The alternate server confirmation example yields `requires_action` with `next_action.type: redirect_to_url`. The integration sends the customer to the URL in `next_action`. P24 PaymentMethods are single-use. The guide describes storing the customer's bank preference separately in your database or Customer metadata (May raw lines 1396–1504).
- P24 requires the customer's agreement to authorize the transaction. The customer can agree on the intermediate P24 page. To skip that page, the merchant must clearly display the prescribed linked regulations and information-obligation wording, obtain the customer's consent, then set `payment_method_options.p24.tos_shown_and_accepted` to `true` (May raw lines 1083–1089, 1552–1561).

### Payment status and fulfillment

The May Elements guide uses browser return to retrieve the PaymentIntent status for display. Its sandbox illustrates successful authentication moving the intent from `requires_action` to `succeeded` and failed authentication moving it to `requires_payment_method` (May raw lines 1278–1289, 1340–1345). The May mobile and Elements guides recommend listening for Stripe's `payment_intent.succeeded` event to trigger business actions such as fulfillment, since client callbacks may be missed or manipulated (May raw lines 308–312, 514–518, 731–735, 1346–1350).

### Statement descriptor

The May mobile and legacy Elements guides allow an optional descriptor of up to 14 characters before confirming the PaymentIntent. The bank record shows it as `/OPT/X/////P24-XXX-XXX-XXX {statement_descriptor}`, with a unique P24 reference (May raw lines 259–261, 450–452, 663–665, 860–862).

payments-p24-accept-a-payment.text: Learn how to accept Przelewy24 (P24), a popular payment method in Poland.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:
Make sure all your `line_items` use the `eur` currency.
feature that’s no longer available in the latest version of Stripe.js.

payments-p24-accept-a-payment.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24/accept-a-payment identifies the guide and links to five variants covering Checkout, Elements, iOS, Android, and React Native (new raw lines 1-18). The 2026-05-03 capture describes a single-use, customer-authenticated redirect and Checkout Sessions limited to payment mode and same-currency, one-time items, with separate Sessions for different currencies. It lists EUR/PLN compatibility and separately instructs EUR for all line items when configuring p24 manually (old raw lines 12-50). The historical mobile and Elements paths use a server-created PaymentIntent with the amount and EUR or PLN and provide its client secret for client confirmation (old raw lines 221-245, 406-430, 618-642, 840-858). The mobile instructions collect billing email. Legacy HTML submits email and two React examples omit it, leaving general API requiredness unresolved (old raw lines 263-274, 454-463, 667-708, 1063-1080, 1139-1158, 1221-1230). Customer agreement to the P24 terms is required for authorization. The May Elements guide allows the merchant to skip the intermediate terms page after displaying the prescribed linked terms and collecting consent, then setting tos_shown_and_accepted (old raw lines 1552-1561). Browser return allows status retrieval. The May guide recommends the payment_intent.succeeded event for business actions (old raw lines 1278-1289, 1340-1350). The revision to source-stripe-p24-accept-payment.md records these scoped historical claims and gives the November variant index a navigation link.
payments-p24-accept-a-payment.Q2: The change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24/accept-a-payment is navigational. The five separate variant links replace the inlined guide in this capture (new raw lines 5-18 and old raw lines 8-50, 124-138, 334-348, 540-552, 819-831). source-stripe-p24-accept-payment.md keeps the May historical scope for Checkout Session mode and line items, EUR/PLN compatibility and the separate manual EUR instructions (old raw lines 20-50), the server/client PaymentIntent handoff, and the optional 14-character descriptor configured before confirmation (old raw lines 221-261, 840-862). Reciprocal wording should distinguish that currency scope, remove the blanket email requirement, and describe React Native return setup conditionally for methods that need a return URL (old raw lines 45-50, 586-609, 757-767, 1063-1080, 1139-1158, 1221-1230). The May warning about p24Bank on the then-latest Stripe.js and customer consent before skipping the P24 terms page remain material (old raw lines 819-825, 892-894, 1552-1561). The server redirect path can leave requires_action, browser return provides a way to retrieve status, and sandbox transitions and webhook guidance establish documented outcomes and fulfillment guidance only. The captures leave current SDK support, account eligibility and actual live payment or settlement unverified (old raw lines 1278-1350, 1396-1500).
